$schema-note: Per-store listing field limits (FR-109, contract L1). These are facts about two products owned by other companies, not about this project: they change without notice and silently truncate rather than erroring. Recorded here once so the gate reads them as data and a store's layout change is a data edit.
$units-note: A field limit is a plain number counted in Unicode code points, or an object {max, unit} where the store counts differently. Only one field does today — Apple measures the keyword field in BYTES, which T066 found by re-reading the specification: 'You can provide up to 100 bytes of content.' For ASCII the two agree, so the current 78-character value is 78 bytes either way. They stop agreeing the moment anyone puts an accented word or a dash in there, and the gate would have permitted a field the store truncates.

documentation.title: App Store Connect Help — App information, and Platform version information
documentation.note: Two pages, because the limits are split across them: name and subtitle are app-level ('no more than 30 characters', 'can't be longer than 30 characters'), while promotional text, description and keywords are version-level ('can't be longer than 170 characters', 'Limited to 4000 characters', 'up to 100 bytes of content'). The single URL recorded before T066 held only the first two. Re-read on the date above; every limit matched what was recorded except the keyword field's unit.

documentation.title: Play Console Help — Create and set up your app; Add preview assets
documentation.note: The URL recorded before T066 was a topic id (…/topic/9866151) and returns 404. These two answer pages are what actually state the limits: title 30 characters or less, short description 80 or less, full description 4,000. Re-read on the date above; every limit matched what was recorded.

assets.$note: What each committed artefact must be for its store to accept it (FR-111, contract L8). Dimensions and alpha are read from the PNG header by the gate — no image dependency (Principle II). Three of these are rejection-at-review conditions rather than cosmetic ones, and each is marked.

listing/assets/icon-ios-1024.png.note: REJECTION CONDITION. Apple rejects an app icon with an alpha channel and one with pre-applied corner rounding. An icon exported from a design tool with a transparent background looks correct everywhere except at submission.

listing/assets/icon-adaptive-foreground..note: The launcher masks this to a shape the device chooses, so every meaningful pixel sits inside the centre safe zone. Transparency is the point here — an opaque foreground defeats the mask.

listing/assets/feature-graphic-1024x500..note: REJECTION CONDITION. Play will not publish a listing without a feature graphic, and it is the asset most easily forgotten because no other store has an equivalent.

apps/mobile/assets/icon.png.requiredBy: the iOS app icon built into the binary
apps/mobile/assets/icon.png.note: REJECTION CONDITION, and a silent one first. Apple rejects an alpha channel, but before a submission ever happens Expo's generateUniversalIconAsync sets removeTransparency:true and an opaque white backgroundColor for this variant — so a transparent source is composited onto WHITE and ships looking merely wrong rather than failing (008 D4). Byte-identical to icon-ios-1024.png by construction; artwork.json records the same digest for both.

apps/mobile/assets/icon-adaptive-foregro.requiredBy: the Android adaptive launcher icon built into the binary
apps/mobile/assets/icon-adaptive-foregro.note: Transparency is the point: the launcher composites this over the background layer below, and an opaque foreground hides that layer entirely. Drawn at the safe-zone scale, unlike the listing copy of the same name, because the mask may be a circle (FR-174).

apps/mobile/assets/icon-adaptive-backgro.requiredBy: the Android adaptive launcher icon built into the binary
apps/mobile/assets/icon-adaptive-backgro.note: A solid --ct-background field, not artwork. It exists so app.config.ts can name a backgroundImage and never a backgroundColor hex string, which would be an ESLint error in apps/** (008 D3). Expo requires it to match the foreground's dimensions.

apps/web/public/apple-touch-icon.png.requiredBy: iOS Safari — Add to Home Screen
apps/web/public/apple-touch-icon.png.note: Three ways to get this wrong, all of which look right in a file browser. SVG is not accepted here at all and degrades to a screenshot of the page. Transparency is filled with solid BLACK. And the source must be SQUARE: icon.svg is generated pre-rounded for a favicon, and iOS masks again, cutting the corners twice (008 D6). 180 is the largest size iOS asks for and it downscales for the rest.

ios.requiredBy: App Store — a 6.9" iPhone set; the store derives the smaller sizes from it
ios.note: The two counts are not the same rule, and T066 added the second. Apple's limit is 10 screenshots per DISPLAY SIZE, and light and dark are one display size to Apple — so `countPerAppearance.max` alone permitted 20 files for a slot that accepts 10. Two are committed today, so nothing was ever wrong in practice; it was a limit encoded against the wrong axis, which is the kind of thing that is only wrong on the day someone needs it.

android.requiredBy: Google Play — 2 to 8 phone screenshots in total
android.note: REJECTION CONDITION. Play requires the longest side to be no more than twice the shortest. A modern phone emulator boots at 1080×2400, which is 2.22:1 and is rejected — so the capture profile is pinned to 1080×1920 (1.78:1) and the gate checks the committed pixels rather than trusting the device profile.
